title: "Trajectory Optimization"
description: "Finding a sequence of states or actions that achieves a goal while minimizing cost and satisfying constraints."
term: "Trajectory Optimization"
letter: "T"
category: "Robotics"
difficulty: "Advanced"

## Simple explanation

Trajectory optimization finds a good path for a system to follow over time.
For a robot, it can choose movements that reach a target while avoiding
obstacles and respecting limits on speed or acceleration.

## Technical explanation

A trajectory optimization problem selects state and control sequences to
minimize an objective subject to dynamics and constraints. The objective
may include goal error, smoothness, energy, or collision penalties.
Methods include direct transcription, sequential quadratic programming,
and sampling-based optimization.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Planning a dynamically feasible trajectory is important in robotics,
autonomous driving, and control. Solutions depend on model accuracy,
constraint handling, computational budget, and replanning frequency.

## How it works

The system discretizes time, represents candidate states and controls,
evaluates cost and constraints, and iteratively searches for a feasible,
low-cost sequence. A controller tracks the plan and may re-optimize as new
sensor observations arrive.

## Practical example

A mobile robot can optimize a short-horizon path that approaches a target,
avoids obstacles, and limits abrupt steering. It replans after receiving
new sensor information rather than assuming the environment remains fixed.

## Common misconceptions

- The shortest geometric path may be dynamically infeasible or unsafe.
- An optimizer can fail to find a global optimum, and a feasible plan still
  requires reliable feedback control.
